references.text: Both verses emphasize Ruth's identity as the one who submits and seeks belonging, either through loyalty to Naomi or by seeking a kinsman-redeemer.
Connects Ruth's search for the human kinsman-redeemer (Goel) with the psalmist's confession that God is the divine Redeemer who frees His servant.
Both verses depict a woman meeting a man who will become her protector/husband with a gesture of submission and respect (veil/feet).
Both verses show how a woman uses the title 'servant' and humble gestures to appeal to a powerful man's protection and grace.
Both verses highlight Ruth's consistent use of 'servant' and acknowledgment of Boaz's kindness, marking the development from seeking grace to seeking a kinsman-redeemer.
